evidence: STYLE_BLOCK `<style\b...>([\s\S]*?)</style>` ran over raw html, so a `<style>` literal inside a JS string was extracted as CSS, and the design comment claimed CSS detectors never saw script content. The agent chose the reviewer's second option (make the claim true by blanking script bodies) rather than documenting the limit, which was the stronger choice.
guidance_note: When a scanner treats a region as raw text for one detector (script bodies are not HTML), apply that to every preprocessing pass over the same input, including comment stripping, not just the detector that was flagged.

evidence: Original STYLE_ATTR `(?:"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)')` had no unquoted alternative while attrValue/srcAttr handle all three forms, so `style=background:url(https://...)` was never scanned. The fix added `([^\s>]+)` and the offset math for the missing quote. The cited law is about one representation per behavior; this is a coverage gap, so the token is decoration.
guidance_note: When several regexes read the same HTML attribute grammar, build them all from one shared attribute-value fragment so every quoting form is covered by construction.

evidence: The original contract suite exercised only the external-resource rejection through store.put; the oversize branch of the same enforcer had no cross-backend case. 91329c1 added it.
guidance_note: When adding a contract test for a gate, write one case per branch of the gate's violation union (external-resource and oversize), not one representative case.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the overclaiming name 'before minting or writing anything' is on the original test (it appears in the round-0 F3 hunk). 91329c1 only added the oversize test beside it. Nothing reachable through the ArtifactStore interface could observe a ghost write, and fd5d45d's spy BlobStore test now checks that writes stays empty.
guidance_note: Name a test only for what its assertions can observe; when the claim is 'nothing was written', assert it with a spy on the write seam in the same commit.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the naive `/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g` strip on STYLE_BLOCK content is original code (the hunk shows it unchanged), and 91329c1 did not touch it. A `/*` inside `url("https://evil/*/x")` opens a fake comment and hides the url(), which is a real false negative. fd5d45d replaced the strip with a string-aware pass.
guidance_note: Before stripping comments with a regex, list the contexts where the opener is data (quoted strings), and write a string-aware pass if any exist.

evidence: The ResourceSink comment listing 'preconnect' is in the original file (hunk @@ -0,0 +1,318), and the agent confirms preconnect had already been removed from FETCH_INITIATING_LINK_RELS before review. So this is pre-review drift, and the ON-NAMED-FIX flag is a false positive. Listing set members in a comment is the 'what' comment that the law targets.
guidance_note: When removing a member from a closed set, grep the file for that member's name and update or delete every comment that enumerates the set.

evidence: This is the test-gap duplicate of F5, about the same pre-existing CSS comment regex, so the flag on 91329c1 is a false positive. fd5d45d added the 'still detects an external url() whose quoted value contains /*' test using the reviewer's input.

fd5d45d touched only storage files. The finalizeSuccess SelfContainmentError catch, with its different create/append disposal, was original code with a test for the create target only, so the flag is a false positive. 70ed281 added the continue-target test asserting failed status, no append, and disposed==[].
guidance_note: When a catch routes through a function whose behavior depends on a discriminant (create vs append), write one test per discriminant value and one for the re-throw branch when the catch is written.

evidence: The `throw error` path for non-SelfContainmentError store failures in the same finalizeSuccess catch had no test. F8's fix (70ed281) added the append-branch test but did not sweep the catch's third branch. 2bea1c5 added the 'disk full' re-throw test.
guidance_note: When a reviewer flags one untested branch of a try/catch, enumerate every branch of that catch (each target kind and the re-throw) and cover all of them in the same fix commit.

evidence: The agent showed that the reviewer's exact example was still caught, because SCRIPT_SRC scanned the un-blanked `scannable`, so the stated mechanism was wrong. The underlying flaw was real: the comment strip ran over script raw text, and `<script>x="<!--"</script><script src=evil></script><!-- -->` evaded the gate. This is the same 'script content is raw text, not HTML' gap that F1's fix handled only for CSS extraction.
guidance_note: When fixing a raw-text-vs-markup confusion for one consumer, reorder the whole preprocessing pipeline to resolve that structure first so every later pass (comment strip, src scan, CSS scan) inherits it.

evidence: In 2bea1c5's cssRegions, stripCssComments(inner) is applied to STYLE_BLOCK regions but `regions.push({ text: value, offset })` for STYLE_ATTR is not stripped, so a commented-out url() in an inline style is falsely flagged. F5's fix (fd5d45d) replaced the strip only at the block call site. Fixed in c15c540.
guidance_note: When replacing a helper at one call site, apply it to every region type the function produces (block and attribute CSS) rather than only the line the reviewer pointed at.

narrative: This PR adds a static self-containment gate at the ArtifactStore seam. Most round-1 and round-2 findings flag pre-existing gaps in the original regex scanner; they carry ON-NAMED-FIX flags only because review anchors to the head commit. The fix-caused findings are all incomplete sweeps: script-as-raw-text fixed for CSS but not for comment stripping (F10), string-aware comment stripping applied to style blocks but not style attributes (F11), and one catch branch tested but not its sibling (F9). Without those three, round 4 would not have occurred.
guidance_observations: The agent fixed each finding at the exact line the reviewer pointed to rather than sweeping the same concern across the sibling regex or branch, which produced three single-instance follow-up findings.

A hand-rolled HTML scanner needs a written list of HTML parsing contexts (script raw text, comments, quoted attributes, CSS strings) before the first regex; each review round here discovered one of them.

evidence: `const POLL_CEILING_MS = 45 * 60 * 1000` had a comment deriving it from '2 × 15 min' while not computing it from DEFAULT_GENERATION_POLICY. Accepting was right, but the fix followed the reviewer's suggestion to derive from the DEFAULTS rather than the runtime policy the server actually reads, which F6/F7 then flagged.
guidance_note: When deriving a client bound from a server policy, derive it from the same runtime source the server reads (the env parse seam), not from the compile-time defaults.

evidence: `await reclaimOnFailure(...)` sat before the try, so a rejection would skip the finally that clears retryInFlight and every later poll would report running. The reviewer admits this is currently unreachable, but the invariant was structurally undefended. 6e8410a moved the whole body under try/finally.
guidance_note: When a finally block clears a single-flight guard, put every await of the guarded body inside that try.

evidence: The Worker hardcoded DEFAULT_GENERATION_POLICY.maxAttempts and ignored the env, which is a real drift. The agent adopted the reviewer's whole cure, including adding TINKERPAD_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS to the edge Env and validating a deadline the edge has no driver to consume. F10 showed this lets an invalid inert value brick the entire Worker; the agent then reversed it in 13002d7.
guidance_note: Before adopting a reviewer's 'parse it here too' cure, check that this composition root consumes every parsed value; parse only what is wired.

evidence: The original catch called finalizeFailure, which re-runs reclaimOnFailure on a handle already reclaimed at the top of beginRetry, so create targets were disposed twice. 6e8410a settles `{state:'failed'}` directly and asserts `h.disposed` has length 1.
guidance_note: When a comment claims an operation is idempotent so it can run twice, add the assertion that proves it (or remove the second call) in the same commit.

evidence: The `generationPolicy: DEFAULT_GENERATION_POLICY` line in app.live.test.ts is the original PR's change (6e8410a does not touch that file), so the ON-NAMED-FIX flag is a false positive. A 15-min × 2 retry under a 15-min vitest ceiling is a real timeout hazard. b4efa7b took the reviewer's no-retry option with a 5-min deadline.
guidance_note: When changing a default that widens worst-case duration, grep for every test timeout and liveness ceiling that bounded the old worst case and recompute them in the same commit.

evidence: 6e8410a computed `DEFAULT_GENERATION_POLICY.timeoutMs * maxAttempts * 1.5`, while the server reads env overrides through parseGenerationPolicy, so an operator raising both knobs puts the server's worst case above the seeder ceiling. F1's fix moved from one hardcoded value to another compile-time value. b4efa7b reads the runtime policy in resolveConfig.
guidance_note: When a reviewer says 'derive X from the policy', identify where the running server gets that policy and derive from that same seam, not the nearest constant.

evidence: This duplicates F6 against the same 6e8410a line. The 6e8410a comment itself conceded the margin covers only 'one env override above the default', and timeoutMs=30min with 2 attempts (60 min) exceeds the 45-min ceiling. Resolved by the same b4efa7b change.

b4efa7b deleted `const POLL_CEILING_MS` but wrote a new comment saying 'The ceiling itself (POLL_CEILING_MS below, in resolveConfig) is DERIVED', naming a constant that no longer exists. The defect is an inaccurate reference, not a what-vs-why comment, so the law token does not fit.
guidance_note: After renaming or deleting a symbol in a fix, grep for the old name, including in the comments you just wrote, before pushing.

evidence: The `maxAttempts: number` field in app.ts is original PR code, so the ON-NAMED-FIX flag is a false positive. The type is looser than its domain, though a runtime guard existed. The agent went beyond the reviewer's request and deleted makeGenerationService's guard, leaving no type or check to stop a non-parsed caller from passing 0. It deferred the branded type to an unnamed 'own ticket' instead of fixing at the parse seam that types-are-the-program points to.
guidance_note: When the law-aligned fix is a narrower type produced by the parse seam, do that; do not delete the only remaining runtime check in the name of single-enforcer while the type still admits the illegal value.

evidence: 6e8410a made the Worker call parseGenerationPolicy, including timeoutMs, inside handlerFor, so an invalid inert TINKERPAD_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS throws on every request and takes down unrelated read-only surfaces. 13002d7 split out parseMaxGenerationAttempts and removed the deadline from the edge Env. The reply-hint 'pushback' is wrong: the agent agreed and fixed.
guidance_note: Before adding boot-time validation to a root, ask what fails if the value is invalid; validating a value the root does not consume widens the blast radius for no benefit.

evidence: b4efa7b inserted `parseGenerationPolicy(...)` into resolveConfig, whose other validations all throw UsageError (exit 2). The parser throws a plain Error, so the fix broke resolveConfig's typed-error contract, and the new test asserted only the message, not the type. 70111e4 wraps the call and rethrows as UsageError.
guidance_note: When calling a new throwing dependency inside a function with a typed-error contract, check how its siblings fail and match that error type, asserting the type in the test.

evidence: parseMaxGenerationAttempts is a one-line call to `parsePositiveInt(value, 'TINKERPAD_MAX_GENERATION_ATTEMPTS', 1, default)`. The existing '0' test already fails if the env-var name or the min argument changes, so the reviewer's claimed blind spot is false. 'soon' and '1.5' only re-test parsePositiveInt, which other tests already cover. The added tests carry cost without catching anything new.

The 'defaults each value independently' test (original file) covered only timeoutMs-set/maxAttempts-unset. The symmetric case is a real but small gap: 13002d7's 'agrees with parseGenerationPolicy' test passes `timeoutMs: undefined, maxAttempts: '3'` but asserts only maxAttempts. The flag is a false positive because this is pre-review test code.
guidance_note: A test named 'each X independently' should cover every X in both directions.

evidence: parsePositiveInt (original code) uses `Number(value)`, which accepts '0x10' (16) and '1e3' (1000), contradicting its integer contract. cd6766b adds a `/^\d+$/` guard. The agent named the identical gap in parseLimit/parsePort and filed tinkerpadai-config-bos to unify them rather than leaving them silently divergent.
guidance_note: When writing an env-int parser, reject anything that is not plain decimal digits before calling Number(), and reuse the repo's existing parser rather than writing a third copy.

narrative: This PR adds a generation deadline and retry policy. Two round-0 fixes generated the PR's later rounds. The seeder ceiling fix derived from compile-time defaults instead of the runtime env (F6/F7), and its follow-up left a dangling comment (F8) and broke resolveConfig's UsageError contract (F11). The Worker fix adopted the reviewer's cure wholesale and validated an unconsumed deadline, which could brick the edge (F10); that led to a new parser and a low-value test request (F12). Round 3 consisted entirely of fix-caused findings.
guidance_observations: The agent adopted reviewers' proposed cures verbatim (derive from DEFAULT, parse timeoutMs at the edge) without checking them against what the running system reads or consumes, and each verbatim cure produced a next-round finding.
The agent accepted every finding, including one whose stated rationale was false (F12), and removed a runtime guard to satisfy a type-tightness finding (F9) instead of tightening the type.

evidence: In the original code, `server.listen` completes before `puppeteer.launch`, and the try/finally that closes the server opens after launch, so a launch failure leaks a listening socket. c423364 nests launch inside an outer try whose finally closes the server. The agent reports verifying that a bad executablePath now exits cleanly.
guidance_note: Open the try/finally for a resource on the line immediately after acquiring it, before acquiring the next resource.

evidence: The original `catch { console.warn(...); return; }` around page.goto passed the artifact on any navigation error, including renderer crashes. c423364 rethrows anything that is not a puppeteer TimeoutError.
guidance_note: Every catch that converts an error into a pass must name the one error type it means; write `catch (e) { if (!(e instanceof X)) throw e; }` from the start.

evidence: handlerFor hardwired passThroughValidator, so no HTTP-layer test drove a FunctionalDefectError to a 200 {state:'failed'} response. c423364 parameterized the validator and added that test. The gap is modest because the serialization is shared, but real.
guidance_note: When adding a new failure kind to a service, add one test at the outermost boundary clients read, not only at the service.

evidence: This duplicates F1: the same server leak when puppeteer.launch throws before the try. It was resolved by the same c423364 restructure.
This is a third duplicate of the F1 server leak, resolved by the same c423364 restructure.

The describe-level `resolveBrowserExecutablePath(process.env)` is in the original live test file (hunk @@ -0,0 +1,56), so the flag is a false positive. Vitest runs a skipped suite's factory at collection. The agent reports reproducing this with TINKERPAD_CHROME_PATH=/nonexistent and moved construction into beforeAll in f870eb6.
guidance_note: In a conditionally-skipped suite, keep the describe body free of effects and put environment probes in beforeAll; verify by collecting with the dependency absent.

evidence: The timeout `return` that discards already-collected pageerrors is in the original code (`catch { console.warn(...); return; }`); c423364 narrowed the catch but kept the return, so this is pre-existing, not caused by that fix. f870eb6 runs the errors check on both paths, with a live throw-then-hang test.
guidance_note: When narrowing a catch, also re-read what the catch body discards (here, the collected errors) before keeping its early return.

evidence: The original interceptor `if (request.isNavigationRequest() && request.frame() === page.mainFrame())` allowed any main-frame navigation, so `window.location = 'https://evil'` reached the network, contradicting its own 'only our origin' comment. It is unchanged by f870eb6, so the flag is a false positive. 878bc71 adds an origin check and a sentinel-server live test.
guidance_note: When an allowlist comment says 'only X', make the predicate test X itself (here the URL origin), not a proxy property that X happens to have.

evidence: The `void request.continue()/abort()` floating promises were original code (unchanged by 878bc71), so the flag is a false positive. The reviewer concedes the risk is low, and the packet does not show whether puppeteer already swallows these rejections. The agent's narrow `.catch(() => undefined)`, with a written argument that the rejection carries no signal about the artifact, is a reasoned exception rather than a blanket swallow.

The reviewer claims a validator crash would let the test pass, but the test is `try { await validator({ html }) } finally { sentinel.close() }` with no catch, so a rejection fails the test, as the agent itself noted. Changing it to `resolves.toBeUndefined()` adds no detection power. The test under review was written in 878bc71 as F8's fix.

narrative: This PR adds a headless-Chrome functional validator. Nearly every finding flags a real defect in the original code: a server leak (three duplicate findings), an over-broad catch, a timeout that discarded observed errors, an unrestricted main-frame navigation, and collection-time effects in a skipped suite. Their ON-NAMED-FIX flags are false positives from head-commit anchoring. The only fix-caused finding (F10) rested on a false premise, and the agent noticed but complied anyway.
guidance_observations: The original resource-lifecycle and catch code had several holes that a pre-push checklist would have caught: every acquired resource needs a covering finally, every pass-on-error catch needs a narrowed type, and every allowlist predicate must test the property its comment names.
When the agent's own reply disproves a reviewer's failure scenario (F10), the right move is to push back rather than make a no-op change to close the thread.
